meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Hale. My son got a zero and nobody called me first. Why?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Go on.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. A student can write somewhere else and paste it in, so that shows me a paste, not who wrote it. Was Owen asked about any of it before the zero went in?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Pull it up. And you skipped my question: was Owen heard before the zero went in?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A bad quotation is a seventeen-year-old getting a line wrong, and you mark those every week. Twice now you've stepped past whether Owen was heard first. I'll take that as a no.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.

Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's called thinking. You keep adding documents and answering nothing I say back. What rules out that he wrote it somewhere else and pasted it in?
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you did speak to him on November 2; fine. A seventeen-year-old cornered by his teacher goes blank, and I'd want to read that note myself. What are you asking for, Hale?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
A timed piece in class against an essay done at home isn't a like-for-like comparison. I asked what you're asking for. Say it.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then it's off the table, and it stays off. Go on.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

Ten minutes. That's 4.4, and I'll take it to put this behind him, not because he did anything: private, not in front of his class, nothing on file, in writing tonight. Copies of your note and that version history go in my email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
It works if the new mark is in before December 1. When does he write it?
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, November 12. Put the time in tonight's email and I'll confirm it with him.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes. Thursday, November 12, the mark in before December 1, and the copies I asked for.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
One thing. Is anything on his record right now, and who else has seen this?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

In our meeting today you agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen this week, not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero well before December 1 and nothing placed on his record. I still want the time for Thursday, November 12, copies of your November 2 note and the version history, and an answer to the question you left open: whether anything is on his record right now and who else has seen this. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight, the time for Thursday, copies of your note and the version history, and an answer on whether anything is on his record now and who else has seen this; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: you told her about your dated November 2 conversation with Owen, which answered the question she had asked twice about whether he was heard before the zero, and it was the first thing she could check that also met her procedural point.
What cost ground: you kept moving to the next document without answering what she said back, including her point that he could have written it elsewhere and pasted it in, so she got shorter and sharper and no single piece stood on its own.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the essay arriving in two large edits between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday October 28, came very close to a late night like that one, which is why she wrote the times down and went straight to procedure; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she told you to pull up the version history and asked what rules out a paste from somewhere else, turn the screen and answer that one point before you bring up the quotation.
